haiku-low.q1: Before ready. Each instance blocks on R1, loading all three secrets at startup, and readiness returns 200 only after that load succeeds.
haiku-low.q2: It makes 4 attempts, exits non-zero, and never becomes ready. The rollout halts and old pods keep serving, so live traffic is unaffected.
haiku-low.q3: A refresh every 5 minutes with jitter reads the latest version and swaps it in if changed. On failure, it keeps the last good value, logs a WARNING, and retries next run.
haiku-low.q4: Only in the in-process SecretCache memory. They must never appear on disk, in environment variables, or in logs.
haiku-low.q5: Only the security on-call writes prod secrets. Engineers cannot read prod values; the orders-api-prod identity reads them at runtime.
haiku-low.q6: Old keys remain in git history, which is not rewritten. They become harmless only after each is rotated at its provider and the old key is revoked.
haiku-low.q7: Each provider call reads the current value from the cache at call time, not from a copy made in the constructor, so refreshed keys are used.
haiku-low.q8: A6 compares each pod's latest loaded or rotated version id with the store's latest, confirms consumers, waits a refresh interval, and checks no old pods or error spikes remain.
haiku-low.q9: Set store access (A1), issue new provider keys (A3), copy keys into the store (A4), switch the app and remove config keys (A5), then revoke old keys (A7).
haiku-low.q10: make run reads sandbox keys from orders-api/dev using the developer's own identity. make run --offline uses stub servers and dummy keys with no store call.
haiku-low.q11: Not found is fatal and not retried. The instance logs an error naming the failing secret, exits non-zero, and never becomes ready, even though the other two loaded.
haiku-low.q12: No cadence is set. Scheduled rotation is not decided and is listed as Open question 1.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded at startup (R1, blocking) before the instance is marked ready; the ready flag is set only after all three secrets load (or offline mode is on).
sonnet.q2: It retries (4 attempts total, 2s apart), then logs an error naming failing secrets and error types and exits non-zero. It never becomes ready, the rollout halts, and old pods keep serving traffic so customers are unaffected.
sonnet.q3: A background refresh every 5 minutes (with jitter) reads the latest version of each secret; if the version id changed and the value is non-empty with no whitespace, it swaps the cache entry and logs 'secret rotated'. If the read or check fails, it keeps the last good value, logs a WARNING (name, last good version id, error type, no value), and retries next run; a staleness alert fires based on fetched_at (threshold undecided).
sonnet.q4: Held only in process memory, in the in-process SecretCache. They must never appear on disk, in environment variables, or in logs (only names and version ids may be logged; value type repr/str is '<redacted>').
sonnet.q5: Read: only the orders-api-prod identity (pods) reads prod values; engineers and the CI deploy identity cannot. Write: only the security on-call writes prod secrets.
sonnet.q6: The leaked keys remain in git history, which is not rewritten. They are made harmless by rotating every key at its provider and revoking the old key (A7) after all instances are confirmed on the new key.
sonnet.q7: The client reads the current value from the SecretCache at call time (e.g. cache.get('payments_api_key')) rather than copying the key in its constructor; the store is never called on the request path.
sonnet.q8: A6: a saved log query plus a script compares, for each pod and secret, the latest 'secret loaded'/'secret rotated' version id against the latest store version id. It also requires every A0 consumer confirmed or stopped, at least 5 minutes plus margin since the last store write, no old-image pod remaining, and normal provider error rates.
sonnet.q9: A0 inventory consumers; A1 set up store, KMS and access; A2 dev store and local dev; A3 issue new keys at providers (rotation); A4 write new keys to prod store; A5 ship new image that reads from the store and removes api_key from config (with CI guard); A6 confirm all instances; A8 block rollback before first revocation; A7 revoke old keys; A9 cleanup.
sonnet.q10: From the dev store path orders-api/dev/* (non-live sandbox keys), read with the developer's own identity, with APP_ENV=dev via make run. Alternatively, make run --offline uses a local stub server and a fixed dummy key in memory, with no store call.
sonnet.q11: It is treated as 'not found', which is fatal at once and not retried; the instance logs an error naming the secret, exits non-zero, and never becomes ready.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. Scheduled rotation is undecided; the plan sets no cadence (Open question 1).
